Issue Details
This is initial MaxStack calculation for simple (no branching) instructions, basically `UpdateStackSize(OpCode opCode)` will be called for each `OpCode` emit and updates the `_currentStack` based on its `StackBehaviourPush`, `StackBehaviourPop` values ```cs private void UpdateStackSize(OpCode opCode) { _currentStack += GetStackChangeFor(opCode.StackBehaviourPush) + GetStackChangeFor(opCode.StackBehaviourPop); if (_currentStack > _maxStackSize) { _maxStackSize = _currentStack; } } ``` This calculation will be updated as needed when branching IL.Emit overloads implemented. Contributes to https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/92975

comments:
Tagging subscribers to this area: @dotnet/area-system-reflection-emit See info in [area-owners.md](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/docs/area-owners.md) if you want to be subscribed.
Issue Details
### Background and motivation [OpCodes](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/Reflection/Emit/OpCodes.cs#L258) represents MS IL instructions that used for emitting IL with [ILGenerator](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.reflection.emit.ilgenerator). An `OpCode` instruction may pop value(s) from stack as an operand of the instruction and also may push value(s) into the stack as a result. This stack change is needed for calculating [MaxStack](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.reflection.methodbody.maxstacksize) value that is essential for populating method body. I could use the `StackBehaviourPop` and `StackBehaviourPush` properties of `OpCode` to calculate this, but there is an internal method that gives this info directly: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/946c5245aea149d9ece53fd0debc18328c29083b/src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/Reflection/Emit/Opcode.cs#L48-L49 Making this public will be useful for calculating `MaxStack` faster Related to https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/93244/files#r1353013060 ### API Proposal ```diff namespace System.Reflection.Emit public readonly partial struct OpCode : System.IEquatable { ... public StackBehaviour StackBehaviourPop { get } public StackBehaviour StackBehaviourPush { get } ... + public int StackDifference() } ``` ### API Usage ```csharp private void UpdateStackSize(OpCode opCode) { _currentStack += opCode.StackDifference(); _maxStackSize = Math.Max(_maxStackSize, _currentStack); } ``` ### Alternative Designs It can be a property too ```diff namespace System.Reflection.Emit public readonly partial struct OpCode : System.IEquatable { ... public StackBehaviour StackBehaviourPop { get } public StackBehaviour StackBehaviourPush { get } ... + public int StackDifference { get } } ``` ### Risks _No response_
Author: buyaa-n
Assignees: -
Labels: `api-suggestion`, `area-System.Reflection.Emit`
Milestone: -
Seems like this should be a property?

> Seems like this should be a property?

Yes, can be a property and that is mentioned in the `Alternative Designs` part

How expensive is the computation?

I assume it's just a switch over the op code as the values are static? In that case I'd be in favor of a property.

I also assume a positive value means the op code net-ads to the evaluation stack (pushing), a negative value means net consumption (popping), and zero means no change or equal amounts of pushing and popping.

If so, I think I'd prefer `EvaluationStackDelta`.

@dotnet/fxdc?

> How expensive is the computation?

The OpCode has this info in the upper 4 bits of `m_flags` field:
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/d18295e107a297dfe4e12ef5b34c28a63548ab31/src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/Reflection/Emit/Opcode.cs#L34
So the computation is just shifting those bits:
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/d18295e107a297dfe4e12ef5b34c28a63548ab31/src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/Reflection/Emit/Opcode.cs#L48-L49


> I also assume a positive value means the op code net-ads to the evaluation stack (pushing), a negative value means net consumption (popping), and zero means no change or equal amounts of pushing and popping.

Yep, that is right
Slightly more verbose, but I think `StackSizeDelta` rings a bit better than `StackDelta` which is somewhat ambiguous.
Another option could be `StackTransitionDelta`, as it is showing the difference of evaluation stack transition/movement, also could be `StackDepthDelta`.
Either of those names work for me :-)

review_comments: Having an aggregate comparison for stack size like this is fine, but may not detect bugs at an opcode level since, for example, an off-by-one in one case may be offset by an opposite off-by-negative-one case. Should we check the current stack size after each Emit(opcode) by using reflection to investigate the current stack size in the generator (`m_curDepth`) or is this redundant in general due to other tests?

> Should we check the current stack size after each Emit(opcode) by using reflection to investigate the current stack size in the generator (m_curDepth) or is this redundant in general due to other tests?

We can check stack size after each Emit(opcode), but might be redundant, especially in this PR only simple Emit operations covered that changes the stack linearly. My plan was keep checking the `MaxStackSize` for next PRs that add more complicated Emit overloads. It might be good to test current stack size for those Emit overloads that change the stack differently.
This condition will handle all negative numbers too, is that what we want? I think an exception or some other other mode would be more appropriate.
I thought when casting to `uint` negative values would become positive large number something that > 3, no?
Yes, that is true. My statement was more related to the notion of all unknown values being converted to `Ldarg_3`. I think `Ldarg_0` or an exception being the failure mode makes more sense.
I am OK with defaulting to `Ldarg_0`, though this is how the existing CoreLib `ILGenerator` does, maybe we should keep it as is for compat, what you think?
Boo. Your instinct here is correct - keep the same behavior.
This needs to mention what this API returns when this is unknown (e.g. for `call` instruction)
